title: Truthfulness of Scripture
definition: The truthfulness of Scripture is the doctrine that God's Word is true in all that it teaches because the God who speaks cannot lie.
summary: Scripture can be trusted because it comes from the faithful and truthful God.
christFocus: Jesus prayed, 'Your word is truth,' and He Himself is the truth to whom Scripture points.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The truthfulness of Scripture flows from the character of God. Since God is true and cannot lie, His Word is trustworthy. Scripture does not merely contain helpful spiritual thoughts; it reveals truth from the God who is faithful in all He says.

This doctrine calls believers to receive Scripture with confidence. When Scripture teaches, warns, promises, commands, or comforts, God's people can trust that His Word is reliable.

The truthfulness of Scripture also confronts deception. Lies about God, sin, salvation, identity, and hope must be answered by what God has spoken.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People are often wounded or confused by false promises, distorted teaching, and changing cultural definitions of truth. The truthfulness of Scripture gives believers a steady place to stand.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When you face confusion, return to Scripture and ask what God has clearly said. Let the truth of the Word correct false beliefs, expose lies, and strengthen your trust in Christ.
